name: topological_sort
author: 63fb3e40
description: Orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so that every edge A->B puts A before B (Kahn's algorithm), grouped into stages: stage 1 has no prerequisites, stage 2 needs only stage-1 nodes, and so on. Use it for questions like 'In what order should these courses be taken?', 'What must I take before Deep Learning, and in what order?' (pass node), 'What is the minimum number of semesters?' (number_of_stages) or 'Does this dependency graph have a cycle?'. Works on directed graphs only (weights are ignored); undirected graphs return an error. Returns is_dag, the order as nodes with position and stage, and stage sizes. If the graph has a cycle, no order exists: it returns is_dag false and a shortest cycle instead.

graph_id.description: Id of the directed graph to order, e.g. 'courses'.

node.description: Optional node id. If given, only this node and everything that must come before it (its ancestors) are ordered, ending with the node itself. Use lookup_node to find ids.

top_k.description: Maximum number of nodes of the order to list (the counts always cover the whole graph).
